title: Existence of minimal finite graded free presentations
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $S=k[x_0,x_1]$ with standard total-degree grading [def-sc-p1-standard], and set $I=(x_0,x_1)$. Let $N$ be an $S$-module internally graded by $\mathbf Z$ with $S_nN_j\subseteq N_{n+j}$, and suppose a finite set of homogeneous elements spans $N$. Then there are a finite graded free $S$-module $F$ with homogeneous basis $e_i$ indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(r)$, degrees $d_i\in\mathbf Z$, and a degree-zero surjective $S$-linear map $q:F\to N$ such that $q^{-1}(IN)\subseteq IF$. These are the data of a minimal graded presentation [def-sc-p1-minimal-graded-presentation], with its target fixed to $N$ and its given grading. No Tor hypothesis is required.

source.place: Graded Hilbert syzygy argument, expanded by the standard minimal-presentation construction in step 1 of DAG node lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-free; not a quoted blueprint proof.

proof.text: Restrict scalars from S=k[x_0,x_1] to k via the constant-polynomial embedding. Prove that f-C(constantCoeff f) lies in I using Mathlib MvPolynomial.mem_pow_idealOfVars_iff' at power 1. Thus every polynomial acts on N/IN by its constant coefficient. A span induction shows the images of the finite homogeneous generating set span the quotient over k. Apply Mathlib exists_linearIndependent to those images, whose finite basis index set is reindexed by Fin r. Choose lifts from the original homogeneous generating set and choose their degrees. This handles the empty quotient basis without a separate case.

Construct F=Fin r →₀ S explicitly, with its standard basis Finsupp.basisSingleOne. Flatten its polynomial coordinates into finitely supported k-coefficients indexed by Fin r × (Fin 2 →₀ ℕ). Define the degree-j subgroup by restricting support to monomials t in coordinate i satisfying degree(t)+d_i=j. These support subsets partition the coefficient index set; disjointness of supported submodules and their supremum being top prove internality, transported through the flattening linear equivalence. The homogeneous product degree formula proves scalar compatibility, and a standard basis vector has degree d_i. Define q by Finsupp.linearCombination S n. For each coefficient of a homogeneous vector, either the coefficient is zero or it is homogeneous of a degree m with m+d_i=j. The given hsmul and the finite sum formula prove q preserves degrees. The local shifted-grading facts follow the already proved construction in Sheaf.RingTheory.GradedFreeCover; that module and its generation theorem are not needed as proof dependencies.

Derive Module.Finite S N from the original finite spanning set. Apply [lem-sc-p1-graded-nakayama-generation] to the lifted quotient basis, obtaining span S (range n)=top. Mathlib span_range_eq_top_iff_surjective_finsuppLinearCombination gives surjectivity of q. If q(a) belongs to IN, its quotient class is zero. Expand a in the standard basis and replace each polynomial action on the quotient by its constant coefficient. Mathlib Fintype.linearIndependent_iff, applied to the chosen quotient basis, forces all constant coefficients to vanish. The power-1 ideal-of-variables criterion puts each polynomial coefficient in I. The finite standard-basis expansion and Submodule.smul_mem_smul show a belongs to IF. All formulas also hold for Fin 0.
